title: Operations and protocol bindings
summary: A2A defines one set of operations (send, stream, get, list, cancel, subscribe, push config, extended card) and exposes them through three functionally equivalent bindings: JSON-RPC, gRPC and HTTP+JSON.
useIf: You implement or call an A2A endpoint and must pick a binding or debug a call across stacks.
avoidIf: You hand-roll the wire format when an SDK exists: the SDK handles method names, headers and streaming for the binding you choose.

explain.md: The spec defines a canonical data model in Protocol Buffers and requires every binding to provide functionally equivalent behaviour [[r1]]. The operations are `SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, `SubscribeToTask`, four push-notification config operations and `GetExtendedAgentCard`. `SendMessage` returns a Task or a direct Message.

explain.md: **JSON-RPC 2.0** runs over HTTP (`application/json`, PascalCase method names). **HTTP+JSON** is REST style and SHOULD use the media type `application/a2a+json`. **gRPC** uses the proto service. Streaming is Server-Sent Events for JSON-RPC and HTTP+JSON and native streams for gRPC. Two service parameters travel as HTTP headers (or gRPC metadata): `A2A-Version` (`Major.Minor`) and `A2A-Extensions`. An unsupported version returns `VersionNotSupportedError`, and an empty header means 0.3 [[r1]] [[r4]].

Which binding you can use is set by the card's ordered `supportedInterfaces` (first is preferred) and by platform limits. Foundry's incoming A2A for v1.0 supports **JSON-RPC only**, text only and no streaming (checked 2026-10-13) [[r17]]. The Agent Framework .NET client prefers HTTP+JSON over JSON-RPC by default and lets you override it with `A2AClientOptions.PreferredBindings` [[r15]]. A `tenant` field lets one endpoint host many agents.

whereToUse: Choosing a binding when you publish an agent for browsers, mobile apps or other services
Calling a Foundry-hosted agent, which accepts only JSON-RPC for v1.0
Debugging a failed call: matching the method or endpoint, version header and media type
Internal high-throughput agent meshes that already run gRPC
Gateway rules that route by path, such as `/message:send`, or by method name

use: JSON-RPC for the widest SDK and platform support, including Foundry
HTTP+JSON when clients are browsers or REST tooling and you want resource-style URLs
gRPC for internal service meshes with typed contracts and native streaming
avoid: Do not assume every peer supports every binding: read the card
Do not omit `A2A-Version`: servers may default to 0.3
Do not build a custom binding unless you can document equivalent error mappings
flips: The peer is Foundry for v1.0: JSON-RPC is the only option
A browser must call the agent directly: HTTP+JSON with SSE is the natural fit
Payload throughput dominates inside one cluster: gRPC reduces overhead

pitfalls.symptom: A client built for v0.3 cannot parse replies from a v1.0 agent
pitfalls.cause: v1.0 uses SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE enums, drops the `kind` discriminator and renames operations (`message/send` became `SendMessage`) [[r2]]
pitfalls.fix: Send `A2A-Version`, read `protocolVersion` per interface and support both versions during migration

pitfalls.symptom: A client picks HTTP+JSON but the server only serves JSON-RPC
pitfalls.cause: The client preferred a binding by default instead of choosing from the card's interfaces
pitfalls.fix: Select from `supportedInterfaces` and set preferred bindings explicitly [[r15]]

pitfalls.symptom: Foundry returns 400 with a version-ambiguous problem
pitfalls.cause: The `A2A-Version` header and the `a2a-version` query value disagreed
pitfalls.fix: Send one selector, or make both equal. With none, Foundry serves 0.3 [[r17]]

scenarios.title: Calling a Foundry-hosted agent
scenarios.situation: Your orchestrator must call an agent hosted in Foundry Agent Service using A2A v1.0. The orchestrator's SDK defaults to HTTP+JSON and wants streaming for a chat UI.
unknowns: Can the UI accept non-streaming replies?
Does the SDK allow preferred bindings?
scenarios.question: What do you configure?

options.name: JSON-RPC, non-streaming, `A2A-Version: 1.0`, Entra token
options.why: It matches what Foundry supports for v1.0: JSON-RPC, text, no streaming.
options.tradeoff: The UI cannot stream tokens from this peer.

options.name: HTTP+JSON with streaming
options.why: Foundry v1.0 does not support HTTP+JSON, gRPC or streaming.
options.tradeoff: Right for peers whose card lists those bindings.

options.name: Put a streaming facade in front of polling
options.why: Keeps the UI responsive while the call stays JSON-RPC.
options.tradeoff: More moving parts and still no token streaming.

flips.if: Foundry later declares streaming for v1.0 on its card
flips.then: Enable SSE after reading the card.
Choose the binding from its card.

scenarios.takeaway: The callee's declared bindings beat the client's default.

scenarios.title: Internal agent mesh at high volume
scenarios.situation: Forty internal agents exchange hundreds of requests per second inside one cluster that already runs gRPC with mutual TLS. Streaming progress is common.
unknowns: Do all agent SDKs support gRPC?
Do any browsers call these agents directly?
scenarios.question: Which binding do you standardize on?

options.name: gRPC with native streaming
options.why: Typed contracts and lower overhead fit an internal mesh that already runs gRPC.
options.tradeoff: Browsers need a gateway and some SDKs may lack gRPC.

options.name: JSON-RPC over HTTP
options.why: Works everywhere and is easier to debug with curl.
options.tradeoff: Higher serialization overhead and SSE instead of native streams.

options.name: A custom binding
options.why: It must define equivalent error mappings and nobody else supports it.
options.tradeoff: Only justified by a transport the three standard bindings cannot use.

flips.if: External partners need to call the agents
flips.then: Offer JSON-RPC or HTTP+JSON at the edge.

scenarios.takeaway: Pick the binding your platform and peers already run.

quiz.q: Match each HTTP+JSON endpoint to its operation.
quiz.explain: The endpoints map one to one to `SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `GetTask` and `CancelTask`.

quiz.q: A client sends no `A2A-Version` header to a server that supports 1.0 and 0.3. Which version does the spec say applies?
options: The latest the client's SDK supports
quiz.explain: An empty version header means 0.3. This is why clients should always send the version explicitly. Servers return `VersionNotSupportedError` for versions they do not support, and 401 is an authentication error.

flashcards.front: Which three bindings does A2A v1.0 define?
flashcards.back: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP, gRPC and HTTP+JSON. All must be functionally equivalent.

flashcards.front: Which binding does a Foundry agent accept for incoming A2A v1.0?
flashcards.back: JSON-RPC only, with text modality and no streaming (checked 2026-10-13).

flashcards.front: What do an empty `A2A-Version` header and an unsupported version mean?
flashcards.back: Empty means 0.3. An unsupported version returns `VersionNotSupportedError`.
